Accuracy bands (±10-25%) are vendor-stated for US/book models WITH proprietary calibration; actual error on uncalibrated amazon.eg estimates is unknown and very likely larger, especially in thin categories.

researchDimensions.topic: Amazon Egypt (amazon.eg) seller economics: referral fees, FBA fees, VAT, and the exact net-profit / margin / ROI formula for a profit calculator
researchDimensions.summary: Amazon Egypt charges a per-category referral fee (most categories a flat % of the total sale price with a 5 EGP minimum; a few categories are tiered, e.g. Electronics Accessories 15% up to 1,000 EGP then 8%, Jewelry 19% up to 5,000 EGP then 5%, Grocery 4%/10% at 250 EGP) plus an FBA fulfillment fee in EGP driven by size-tier and weight (smallest band ~19.5 EGP/unit, with a higher rate when item price exceeds ~350 EGP). Egypt's standard VAT is 14%; critically, Amazon's official pricing page states all fees are shown excluding VAT and 14% VAT is added on top of every fee, while the customer-facing selling price on amazon.eg is VAT-inclusive. There is currently no monthly Professional-plan subscription fee (promotional waiver) and monthly FBA storage is ~4 EGP per cubic foot. Inbound shipping to Amazon's Egypt fulfillment centers is seller-arranged and not published by Amazon, so it must be a user-entered input. The calculator must compute referral fee from the tier rules, add 14% VAT to (referral + FBA + storage) fees, strip output VAT from the sale price when the seller is VAT-registered, and output net profit/unit, margin %, ROI %, and break-even price.
keyFindings: Referral fees are PER CATEGORY on amazon.eg, charged on the total sales price (item price, and Amazon's fee schedule applies it to the item + any shipping the seller charges). Minimum referral fee is 5 EGP for almost all categories. Source: https://sell.amazon.eg/pricing

Flat-rate category examples (single tier, min 5 EGP): Apparel 12%, Beauty 12%, Shoes 12%, Watches 12%, Automotive 12%, Office Products 12%, Luggage 12%, Consumer Electronics 8%, Books 7%, Camera 7%, Small Appliances 7%, Baby 9%, Health & Personal Care 11.5%, Kitchen 11.5%, Sports 11.5%, Home 13%, Furniture 13%, Outdoor 13%, Perfumes 13%, Toys 13%, Pet Products 14%, Tools & Home Improvement 11%, Video & DVD 11%, Personal Care Appliances 11%, 'All Other Categories' 10%.

Low-fee electronics categories (min 5 EGP): Mobile Phones 4.5%, Televisions 4.5%, Home Entertainment 4.5%, Major Appliances 4.5%, Personal Computers 4%, Video Game Consoles 4%. (Mobile Phones rose to 4.5% from 4% and Major Appliances/TV/Home Entertainment to 5% from 4% effective June 16, 2025; a Dec 15 2025-Jun 30 2026 promo reduces Major Appliances/Home Entertainment/Television to 4.5%.)

TIERED categories (the calculator must implement the breakpoint math): Electronics Accessories & Portable Audio & Wireless = 15% on the portion up to 1,000 EGP + 8% on the portion above 1,000 EGP; Jewelry = 19% up to 5,000 EGP + 5% above; Grocery = 4% on the portion up to 250 EGP + 10% above (Grocery has no 5 EGP minimum).

FBA (Fulfillment by Amazon) fee is a per-unit EGP fee by size tier and weight. Minimum/entry rate ~19.5 EGP/unit for the smallest items; Amazon's table shows TWO columns per weight band: a lower fee when item price is below ~350 EGP and a higher fee above ~350 EGP (e.g. Small Envelope <=0.1kg: 19.5 EGP below 350 EGP / 24.5 EGP above 350 EGP). Source: https://sell.amazon.eg/pricing

FBA Standard Parcel ladder (below/above 350 EGP price), EGP per unit: <=0.25kg 19.5/24.5; <=0.5kg 20.5/25.5; <=1kg 21/26; <=2kg 22.5/27.5; <=5kg 25.5/30.5; <=10kg 30.5/35.5; <=12kg 32.5/37.5. Oversize starts ~25/30 EGP at <=1kg and rises to ~83/88 EGP at <=30kg, then +2 EGP per kg above 30kg.

Easy Ship (seller stores, Amazon delivers) fee is separate and higher: standard parcels first 250g = 45.5 EGP, up to 500g 51 EGP, up to 1kg 53 EGP, +2 EGP per extra 500g up to 22kg; oversize first 1kg 55.5 EGP +2 EGP/kg. Customer shipping charge is capped at 26 EGP per shipment.

VAT: Egypt standard VAT rate is 14%. Amazon's pricing page states explicitly: 'All listed fees are displayed excluding applicable VAT. We will additionally apply VAT to all fees displayed above.' So referral fee, FBA fee, and storage fee each get +14% VAT charged to the seller. Sources: https://sell.amazon.eg/pricing and https://aws.amazon.com/tax-help/egypt/

Customer-facing selling prices on amazon.eg are displayed VAT-INCLUSIVE (consumer marketplace). If the seller is VAT-registered, the 14% output VAT embedded in the sale price is remitted to the tax authority and is NOT seller revenue: net-of-VAT price = sale price / 1.14. A VAT-registered seller can reclaim the 14% input VAT charged on Amazon's fees, so those fees are effectively net-of-VAT for them.

VAT registration in Egypt is mandatory at annual turnover of EGP 500,000 (~USD 10,500). Below that threshold a seller is typically not VAT-registered: they do not add/remit output VAT but also cannot reclaim the 14% VAT on Amazon fees, so for them the fee VAT is a real cost. Egypt de minimis on imports is 0 EGP (duty+VAT charged on every import). Source: https://www.sitruna.com/post/how-to-sell-on-amazon-egypt-a-sellers-guide-to-amazon-eg ; https://zonos.com/docs/guides/country-guides/egypt

Monthly subscription: Professional selling plan currently has NO monthly subscription fee ('available with no monthly subscription fee' promotional note on the pricing page). Treat as 0 EGP/month but keep it as a configurable input divided across units.

Monthly FBA storage fee is ~4 EGP per cubic foot per month. This is a periodic cost; to put it per-unit, multiply unit volume (cubic feet) x 4 EGP x expected months in storage. Source: https://sell.amazon.eg/pricing

Inbound shipping / freight to Amazon Egypt fulfillment centers is NOT published by Amazon and is seller-arranged (domestic courier or freight). It must be a user-entered per-unit input (total inbound freight / units in shipment). Same for any import duty if goods are imported (de minimis is 0).
researchDimensions.egyptSpecifics: amazon.eg is a live Amazon marketplace with its own fee schedule denominated in EGP (https://sell.amazon.eg/pricing). Confirmed Egypt-specific facts: (1) Referral fees and the 5 EGP minimum are set per category as listed above; tiered categories use EGP breakpoints (1,000 / 5,000 / 250 EGP). (2) FBA fees are in EGP with a price-band split at ~350 EGP (lower fee for cheaper items). (3) Egypt VAT is 14% and Amazon ADDS 14% on top of all its fees (explicit on the pricing page) — this is the single biggest thing most calculators get wrong. (4) Consumer prices on amazon.eg are VAT-inclusive, so a VAT-registered seller's true revenue is sale_price/1.14. (5) VAT registration threshold EGP 500,000/yr; import de minimis 0 EGP. (6) No monthly Pro-plan fee at present. Fee figures were read from the official pricing page on 2026-06-08; Amazon periodically revises them (notable changes May 1 2025 and June 16 2025, plus a Dec 15 2025-Jun 30 2026 promo), so the calculator should treat all rates as editable config, not hard-coded constants.
researchDimensions.implementationNotes:
DATA STRATEGY (free/scraping): hard-code a versioned fee table seeded from https://sell.amazon.eg/pricing (referral % + min per category; tier breakpoints; FBA EGP ladder by size-tier/weight/price-band; storage 4 EGP/cu.ft/mo; VAT 14%). Re-scrape that single page on a schedule to refresh; do NOT rely on a paid fees API.

INPUTS the calculator must accept (per unit unless noted):
- buy_cost (COGS landed per unit, EGP)
- sell_price (the price shown to the customer on amazon.eg, VAT-INCLUSIVE, EGP)
- category (selects referral rule)
- size_tier + unit_weight_kg + (derived) unit_volume_cuft  -> selects FBA fee
- fulfillment_method: FBA | EasyShip | MFN (self-ship)
- inbound_shipping_per_unit (EGP, user-entered; = total inbound freight / units)
- months_in_storage (for FBA storage), default e.g. 1
- monthly_subscription (EGP, default 0) and units_per_month (to amortize) -> subscription_per_unit
- seller_vat_registered: boolean
- optional: ad_cost_per_unit (PPC/ACoS), return_rate %, other_costs

CORE FORMULAS (implement exactly):
1) referral_fee:
   - flat category: ref = max(rate * sell_price, 5)
   - tiered (e.g. Electronics Accessories): ref = 0.15*min(sell_price,1000) + 0.08*max(sell_price-1000,0); then ref = max(ref, 5)
   - Jewelry: 0.19*min(sell_price,5000) + 0.05*max(sell_price-5000,0); min 5
   - Grocery: 0.04*min(sell_price,250) + 0.10*max(sell_price-250,0); NO minimum
2) fba_fee = lookup(size_tier, weight, price_band) where price_band = (sell_price < 350 ? low : high). For MFN, fba_fee = 0 and seller pays own outbound shipping (separate input).
3) storage_fee = unit_volume_cuft * 4 * months_in_storage
4) amazon_fees_ex_vat = referral_fee + fba_fee + storage_fee
5) fee_vat = 0.14 * amazon_fees_ex_vat
   - effective_fee_cost = seller_vat_registered ? amazon_fees_ex_vat : (amazon_fees_ex_vat + fee_vat)   // registered sellers reclaim the VAT
6) net_revenue = seller_vat_registered ? (sell_price / 1.14) : sell_price   // strip output VAT only if registered/remitting
7) total_cost = buy_cost + effective_fee_cost + inbound_shipping_per_unit + subscription_per_unit + ad_cost_per_unit + other_costs

OUTPUTS:
- net_profit_per_unit = net_revenue - total_cost
- margin_pct = net_profit_per_unit / net_revenue * 100            // margin on (net) revenue
- roi_pct = net_profit_per_unit / buy_cost * 100                  // return on the cash tied up in inventory (COGS); optionally / total_cash_invested
- break_even_price (VAT-inclusive price at which net_profit = 0):
   For VAT-registered seller with a flat referral rate r:
     Let fixed = fba_fee + storage_fee + inbound + subscription + ads + other (these are net-of-VAT for registered seller)
     net_revenue = P/1.14 ; referral_ex_vat = r*P
     Solve P/1.14 - r*P - (buy_cost + fixed) = 0  ->  P*(1/1.14 - r) = buy_cost + fixed  ->  P = (buy_cost + fixed) / (1/1.14 - r)
   For non-registered seller (fees carry VAT, no output-VAT strip):
     P*(1 - 1.14*r) = buy_cost + 1.14*(fba+storage) + inbound + subscription + ads + other  -> solve for P
   For tiered categories, solve break-even numerically (bisection) because referral is piecewise-linear in P.
   Always guard: if denominator <= 0 (referral rate >= net-revenue factor) the product can never break even -> flag.

VALIDATION/EDGE CASES: enforce referral 5 EGP minimum AFTER computing %, apply 350 EGP FBA price-band on the actual sell_price, recompute break-even with the band that applies at that price (the band can flip around 350 EGP), and surface fee_vat as a visible line so users see the 14% uplift. Make every rate editable (store as config with an 'as-of' date) because Amazon revised fees in 2025 and runs promos into mid-2026.
notVerified: Exact FBA EGP fee for every single size-tier/weight cell was read from the live pricing page via an automated fetch; spot-confirm the full ladder directly against https://sell.amazon.eg/pricing before hard-coding, as the page is dynamic and Amazon updates it.
The precise 'price band' threshold for the FBA low/high fee columns is shown as ~350 EGP; confirm the exact cutoff and whether it is < or <= on the official page.

Whether referral fee is charged on item-price-only vs item-price-plus-seller-shipping on amazon.eg specifically (Amazon's global rule is on total sales price incl. shipping for most categories) was not isolated for Egypt — verify on the Egypt fee schedule.
Typical inbound shipping / freight cost to Amazon Egypt fulfillment centers — Amazon does not publish this; it is seller-arranged and must be user-entered. No reliable benchmark EGP figure verified.
Import duty rates (for sellers importing inventory) and any partner-carrier program (AGL) rates into Egypt were not verified; de minimis is confirmed 0 EGP so duty+VAT apply on imports.
Current monthly Professional-plan subscription fee is shown as waived ('no monthly subscription fee') promotionally; verify whether/when a standard monthly fee (and its EGP amount) resumes.

Whether a VAT-registered seller can fully reclaim input VAT on Amazon fees in practice (vs. partial/zero-rated treatment) should be confirmed with an Egyptian tax advisor; treated here as fully reclaimable.

researchDimensions.topic: Free/open Arabic + English review sentiment & theme extraction pipeline for Amazon Egypt (amazon.eg), 2026
researchDimensions.summary: For a free (no paid API) pipeline on amazon.eg reviews, the winning stack is HuggingFace transformers for sentiment + KeyBERT/BERTopic for themes, all MIT/Apache-licensed and runnable on CPU. The single best lever is language/dialect routing: detect each review's language, send Arabic (incl. Egyptian dialect "Masry") to a MARBERT-family fine-tune (UBC-NLP/MARBERTv2 is the dialect-strongest Arabic encoder), and send English reviews to a lightweight DistilBERT-SST2 or cardiffnlp twitter-roberta model. CAMeL Tools gives you a batteries-included Arabic toolkit (sentiment + dialect ID + normalization) but its bundled CAMeLBERT-DA sentiment model underperforms MARBERT on dialectal data, so use CAMeL Tools for preprocessing/dialect-ID and MARBERT for the actual classification. The hard part is Egyptian colloquial Arabic, Franco-Arabic (Arabizi like "3ayez", "msh helw"), code-switching, and sarcasm — MSA-only models fail here, so a dialect-pretrained model plus normalization is mandatory. Theme/complaint summaries are best done extractively and cheaply (KeyBERT keyphrases + aspect grouping + most-frequent-negative-sentence selection) rather than with a generative LLM, keeping the whole thing free and CPU-friendly.
keyFindings: SENTIMENT (Arabic, recommended primary): MARBERT / MARBERTv2 (UBC-NLP, github.com/UBC-NLP/marbert) is pretrained on ~1B dialectal+MSA Arabic tweets and is the strongest open encoder for DIALECTAL Arabic, which is exactly what Amazon Egypt reviews are. Use a sentiment fine-tune such as Ammar-alhaj-ali/arabic-MARBERT-sentiment (3 labels: positive/negative/neutral; ~547 downloads/mo) or fine-tune MARBERTv2 yourself on ASTD/ArSAS. Apache/MIT-style open weights, free.

Ready-to-use Arabic snippet (no training): `from transformers import pipeline; sa = pipeline('text-classification', model='Ammar-alhaj-ali/arabic-MARBERT-sentiment'); sa(['لقد استمتعت بالحفلة','خدمة المطعم كانت محبطة'])` returns label+score (e.g. positive 0.958, negative 0.916).

AraBERT (aubmindlab/bert-base-arabertv2) is the other major free Arabic encoder; strong on MSA, slightly weaker than MARBERT on heavy dialect. Good fallback / ensemble member. PRAli22/AraBert-Arabic-Sentiment-Analysis is a ready sentiment fine-tune. 2025 RANLP AHaSIS shared task confirms transformer fine-tunes (AraBERT/MARBERT) are SOTA for Arabic-dialect sentiment.

CAMeL Tools (github.com/CAMeL-Lab/camel_tools, NYU Abu Dhabi, MIT) = all-in-one free Arabic toolkit: preprocessing/normalization, morphology, DIALECT IDENTIFICATION, NER, and a sentiment analyzer (pos/neg/neutral). Pip-installable; has CLI + Python API. Best used for normalization + dialect-ID, not as the final sentiment model.

CAMeLBERT-DA sentiment (CAMeL-Lab/bert-base-arabic-camelbert-da-sentiment) is BERT-base (~110M), fine-tuned on ASTD+ArSAS+SemEval, but only BINARY (positive/negative) and benchmarks show it underperforms MARBERT/AraBERT on dialectal sentiment. Very popular (~145k downloads/mo) but not the accuracy leader. Snippet: `pipeline('text-classification', model='CAMeL-Lab/bert-base-arabic-camelbert-da-sentiment')`.

EGYPTIAN-DIALECT SPECIFIC: EgyBERT (arxiv 2408.03524, 2024) is pretrained specifically on Egyptian-dialect corpora and beats general Arabic models on Egyptian tasks — strongest option if you fine-tune for amazon.eg's Masry reviews, though you must train a sentiment head (no turnkey pipeline). MARBERTv2 dialect classifier (IbrahimAmin/marbertv2-arabic-written-dialect-classifier, trained on ~850k sentences, 9 dialects incl. Egyptian) can pre-tag reviews as Egyptian vs MSA.

DIALECT CHALLENGE (the core risk): amazon.eg reviews mix (a) MSA, (b) Egyptian colloquial 'Masry', (c) Franco-Arabic/Arabizi in Latin letters ('el-product da 3agbni gdn', 'msh helw', 'wesel bsor3a'), (d) Arabic+English code-switching, (e) emoji/elongation ('حلـــــــو'), and (f) sarcasm/negation. MSA-only or English-only models silently mislabel these. Mitigations: Arabic normalization (alef/ya/ta-marbuta, diacritic + tatweel removal via CAMeL Tools), an Arabizi-to-Arabic transliteration step, and a dialect-pretrained model.

SENTIMENT (English reviews on amazon.eg): use a small CPU model. distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english = ~91.3% SST-2 acc, 40% smaller/faster than BERT, binary pos/neg. cardiffnlp/twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest = 3-class (neg/neu/pos), trained on ~124M tweets, better on short informal review text. VADER (lexicon, NLTK) is ~83% but instant/zero-model — good cheap pre-filter, weak on nuance.

ENGLISH lexicon fallbacks: VADER (vaderSentiment / NLTK, free) and TextBlob are rule/lexicon-based, no GPU, handle emoji/punctuation/caps emphasis; accuracy lower (~80-83%) than transformers. Best role: ultra-cheap first pass or for tie-breaking, not primary scoring.

THEME / KEYWORD EXTRACTION (free): KeyBERT (github.com/MaartenGr/KeyBERT, MIT) extracts keyphrases via embeddings; for Arabic+English use multilingual embeddings (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2). Reported ~80.95% on Arabic keyword extraction vs ~81-82% for AraBERT variants. Use MMR + ngram_range=(1,3) + Arabic & English stopword lists to get clean 'battery life', 'عمر البطارية', 'shipping', 'الشحن' phrases.

RECURRING-THEME clustering (free): BERTopic (also MaartenGr) on multilingual sentence embeddings clusters thousands of reviews into topics (delivery, price, quality, fake/original, sizing) and gives representative keywords per cluster — ideal for 'recurring themes per product/category'. For a single product with few reviews, skip BERTopic and just use KeyBERT keyphrase frequency.

PROS/CONS + COMPLAINT SUMMARY (free, extractive — avoid paid LLM): split reviews by predicted sentiment, run KeyBERT on the positive set -> top phrases = PROS, on the negative set -> top phrases = CONS/complaints, then pick the most representative actual sentences per phrase as evidence quotes. This is deterministic, cheap, bilingual, and needs no generative model. Optional free abstractive upgrade: a small mT5/AraT5 summarizer, but it raises runtime cost.

ASPECT-BASED option: map keyphrases to fixed aspect buckets (Quality, Price/Value, Shipping/Delivery, Authenticity/Counterfeit, Packaging, Seller/Service, Battery, Sizing) and compute per-aspect sentiment by averaging sentiment of sentences containing each aspect's terms (bilingual lexicon). Gives a structured per-product pros/cons table without ML aspect extractors.

RESOURCE / RUNTIME: All weights are free + downloadable. BERT-base/MARBERT/AraBERT ~110M params -> ~420-500MB on disk, ~1-2GB RAM; run on CPU. DistilBERT ~66M is ~2x faster. CPU throughput roughly tens to low-hundreds of reviews/sec batched (GPU optional, 10-50x). KeyBERT/BERTopic embeddings (MiniLM, ~80-120MB) are the lightweight part. VADER/TextBlob are near-instant, negligible memory. Whole stack fits on a free-tier/small VPS; only cost is CPU time + ~1-2GB model storage.
researchDimensions.egyptSpecifics: amazon.eg reviews are overwhelmingly Egyptian-context: a mix of Modern Standard Arabic, Egyptian colloquial 'Masry', Franco-Arabic/Arabizi written in Latin letters and digits ('3', '7', '2' for Arabic letters, e.g. '3ayez', 'msh 7elw', 'wesel bsor3a'), Arabic-English code-switching, plus English-only reviews. This makes a Modern-Standard-Arabic-only OR English-only sentiment model insufficient on its own — you MUST route by detected language/script and use a DIALECT-pretrained Arabic model (MARBERTv2, or EgyBERT for maximum Egyptian fidelity if you fine-tune). Egypt-relevant recurring review themes to bucket: counterfeit vs original ('مقلد' / fake), delivery speed and courier issues, cash-on-delivery, price/value in EGP, packaging damage, and seller trust — these should be your fixed aspect categories. No amazon.eg-specific public sentiment benchmark was found (Not verified); validate on a small hand-labeled sample of real amazon.eg reviews before trusting class accuracy.
researchDimensions.implementationNotes:
PIPELINE (all free, CPU-OK):
1) Ingest scraped reviews (text, star rating, lang-unknown). Keep star rating as a weak sentiment label / sanity check.
2) NORMALIZE + DETECT: use CAMeL Tools (`camel_tools`) for Arabic normalization (Unicode dediac, remove tatweel/U+0640, normalize alef اأإآ->ا, ya ى->ي, ta-marbuta ة); detect script/language (e.g. fastText lid.176 or langdetect, both free) to route. If text is Latin-script Arabizi, optionally transliterate to Arabic (CAMeL Tools transliteration / a Franco-to-Arabic mapping) before classifying.
3) DIALECT ROUTE (optional but recommended): IbrahimAmin/marbertv2-arabic-written-dialect-classifier to tag Egyptian vs other — lets you report dialect coverage and catch mis-routes.
4) SENTIMENT:
   - Arabic -> `pipeline('text-classification', model='Ammar-alhaj-ali/arabic-MARBERT-sentiment')` (3-class) OR fine-tune MARBERTv2/AraBERTv2/EgyBERT on ASTD+ArSAS for best dialect accuracy.
   - English -> `pipeline('sentiment-analysis', model='distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english')` or `cardiffnlp/twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest` (3-class).
   - Map all to {positive, neutral, negative}; cross-check against star rating (1-2 star + positive label = flag for review).
5) THEMES: embed reviews with `paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` (sentence-transformers, free). Per product: KeyBERT keyphrases, `keyphrase_ngram_range=(1,3)`, `use_mmr=True`, `diversity=0.6`, Arabic+English stopwords. Across a category / many reviews: BERTopic on the same embeddings for recurring topics.
6) PROS/CONS + COMPLAINTS (extractive, deterministic): partition sentences by sentiment; KeyBERT on positive set -> PROS list, on negative set -> CONS/complaints list; attach the highest-similarity real sentence as an evidence quote per phrase; rank phrases by frequency. Map phrases to fixed aspect buckets (Quality, Price/EGP value, Shipping/Delivery, Authenticity/counterfeit, Packaging, Seller/service, Battery, Sizing) and compute per-aspect % positive. Optional abstractive summary via AraT5/mT5 (free) only if you accept extra runtime.
LIBS (all free, pip): transformers, torch (CPU build), sentence-transformers, keybert, bertopic, camel-tools, nltk(vaderSentiment), langdetect/fasttext, arabic-stopwords. 
COST: model downloads one-time (~0.4-0.5GB per BERT model, ~0.1GB embedder); RAM ~1-2GB; pure-CPU inference fine for batch nightly jobs; GPU only needed if real-time at scale. Batch with `pipeline(..., batch_size=32)` and truncate to 128-256 tokens (reviews are short) to maximize CPU throughput.
VALIDATION: hand-label ~200 real amazon.eg reviews (mix MSA/Masry/Arabizi/English) and report macro-F1 per language bucket before production — published model F1s are on tweets, not amazon.eg.
notVerified: Exact macro-F1/accuracy of MARBERT vs AraBERT vs CAMeLBERT on Egyptian-dialect sentiment specifically (PeerJ cs-2644 ensemble paper returned HTTP 403; numbers quoted secondhand from search snippets only).
No public sentiment benchmark exists for amazon.eg reviews specifically — class accuracy on real amazon.eg text is unverified and must be measured on a hand-labeled sample.
Reported model accuracies (DistilBERT 91.3% SST-2, twitter-roberta, KeyBERT ~80.95% Arabic) are from their own/general benchmarks, not from Amazon Egypt review data.

EgyBERT has no confirmed turnkey sentiment-classification pipeline on HuggingFace; using it for Egyptian sentiment likely requires fine-tuning a head (not verified that a ready pos/neg/neutral EgyBERT sentiment model is published).

Current (2026) license/redistribution terms and any download-count changes for each HuggingFace model were not re-verified line-by-line; treat licenses as 'open but confirm before commercial deployment'.
Precise CPU throughput (reviews/sec) depends on hardware and was not benchmarked here — figures given are order-of-magnitude estimates.

researchDimensions.topic: Competitive UI teardown of Helium 10, Jungle Scout, Keepa & SmartScout → Screen inventory + component/KPI spec for an Amazon Egypt (amazon.eg) product-research app (Next.js + shadcn/ui + Tailwind, RTL-ready, free/scraping data)
researchDimensions.summary: The four reference tools converge on the same six screen archetypes: (1) an opportunity/niche dashboard, (2) a filterable product database table, (3) a keyword/demand explorer, (4) a product-detail page anchored by a Keepa-style multi-axis history chart, (5) a trend/movers view, and (6) a profit/FBA calculator. Their UI DNA is: dense sortable data-grids with 12-25 columns, a large left/top filter rail with numeric min-max ranges + multi-select chips + presets, a small set of composite scores (Opportunity/Niche Score 1-10, Competition Low→Very High, LQS), and dual-Y-axis time-series charts overlaying price + BSR + units-sold. For amazon.eg specifically you cannot buy data (Helium 10/JS/Keepa/SmartScout do NOT cover Egypt), so every KPI must be derived from scraped Best Sellers / Movers & Shakers / search / product pages plus BSR→sales estimation, with prices in EGP and a full RTL/Arabic mirror. The deliverable below is a concrete 11-screen inventory with shadcn component mapping, a master KPI catalogue, chart-type choices, and Arabic/RTL rules.
keyFindings: SIX UNIVERSAL SCREENS (all 4 tools share these): (a) Opportunity/Niche dashboard — Jungle Scout 'Opportunity Finder', Helium 10 'Black Box', SmartScout 'Category/Brand' explorers; (b) Product Database grid; (c) Keyword/demand tool — H10 Cerebro/Magnet, JS Keyword Scout; (d) Product detail w/ history chart — Keepa is the canonical pattern; (e) Trend/Movers; (f) Profit/FBA calculator. Build all six, plus auth/list/settings shells.

PRODUCT DATABASE GRID columns to replicate (union across H10 Black Box + JS Product DB): thumbnail, Title, ASIN, Brand, Category/Subcategory, Price, Monthly Sales (units), Monthly Revenue, Net/Estimated Revenue (after fees), BSR (rank), Review Count, Star Rating, Review Velocity, Sales-to-Reviews ratio, Weight/Dimensions, Seller Type (FBA/FBM/AMZ), Active Sellers count, Date First Available, LQS/Listing Quality, Images count, growth/trend sparkline. JS also itemizes FBA Fees + Net Profit per Sale inline.

FILTER RAIL pattern (identical across tools): numeric MIN-MAX paired inputs for Price, Monthly Sales, Revenue, BSR, Review count, Rating, Weight; multi-select for Category/Subcategory + Seller Type/Fulfillment; keyword INCLUDE and EXCLUDE text fields; Date-First-Available range; and one-click PRESET chips. JS presets: 'High Demand', 'Low Competition', 'Bad Marketing', 'Poor Products', 'Good ROI'. H10 Black Box toggles Basic↔Advanced filter mode grouped as Product / Competitors / Sales.

COMPOSITE SCORES are the headline KPIs: Jungle Scout Opportunity/Niche Score = 1-10 (10 best) computed from demand + competition + listing quality; Competition rendered as 5-tier categorical (Very Low / Low / Medium / High / Very High); JS LQS = Listing Quality Score; SmartScout uses competition level + dominant-seller-share. We must invent our own EGP-market equivalents because none cover Egypt.

KEEPA CHART is the product-detail centerpiece and the most-imitated component: a dual/triple-axis time-series — LEFT axis = price ($ / EGP), RIGHT axis = Sales Rank/BSR (inverted feel: lower=better). Distinct color-coded series: Amazon price, New price, Used, Buy Box price (pink line), Sales Rank (green), and Units-Sold/month (gold/yellow). Range selector chips: Day / Week / Month / 3 Months / Year / All. Toggles to show/hide each series. Keepa now also surfaces an estimated 'Monthly Sold' count derived from inventory snapshots.

KEYWORD/DEMAND tool KPIs (H10 Magnet/Cerebro + JS Keyword Scout + JS Opportunity Finder): exact Monthly Search Volume, 30-day & 90-day Search-Volume Trend (the 90-day window de-seasonalizes), Competition/keyword difficulty, organic rank, sponsored/PPC presence, CPC bid estimate, Title Density, word/phrase count, and a Seasonality strip (month-to-month spikes vs evergreen). Magnet DB cited at 450M+ keywords; reverse-ASIN (Cerebro) returns the keyword set a competitor ranks for.

TREND / MOVERS view = Amazon's own 'Movers & Shakers' (biggest 24h BSR % gainers) + New Releases + Most Wished For, plus SmartScout-style historical 'search term growth' and brand-share movement. Presented as ranked lists with rank-change arrows (▲▼ + delta), % change badges (green up / red down), and small sparklines. This is the most scrape-friendly demand proxy for amazon.eg.

PROFIT/FBA CALCULATOR fields (JS FBA Profit Calculator pattern): INPUTS — Sale Price, Product/COGS cost, Inbound Shipping, Amazon Referral fee %, FBA fulfilment fee, monthly Storage fee, est. Returns %, PPC/ad cost per unit; OUTPUTS — Net Profit per unit, Profit Margin %, ROI %, and break-even. Display as two-column form (inputs left) → live result card (right) with a fee waterfall. Egypt has no public FBA-fee API, so referral % and fulfilment must be user-editable assumptions.

SmartScout adds a distinct BRAND/SELLER intelligence layer absent in the others: searchable brand database filterable by est. monthly revenue, # of FBA sellers, dominant-seller share, in-stock rate, avg product size, avg selling price; brand dashboards show revenue, subcategory distribution (treemap/donut), and revenue-share-by-seller. Six nav groups: Category, Brand, Seller, Product, Keyword, Learning. Worth a lightweight 'Brand/Seller' screen if scraping permits.

DATA-DENSITY & UX conventions shared by all: sticky table header + sticky first (image/title) column, column show/hide + reorder, row-checkbox multi-select to push selected ASINs into the next tool (H10 'send to Cerebro', 'add to My List'), inline sparkline trend columns, server-side pagination, CSV export, and a persistent saved-filters/'My List' concept. Numbers are right-aligned, monospace-tabular; deltas use color + arrow, never color alone.

AMAZON EGYPT (amazon.eg) SPECIFICS: marketplace = Souq rebranded; #1 marketplace in Egypt (Apr 2026), ahead of Temu & Noon; currency EGP (must format as 'ج.م' / 'EGP' with Arabic-Indic numeral option); pays via card + cash-on-delivery; free delivery > EGP 350. Categories present: Electronics, Mobiles, Fashion/Apparel, Home & Kitchen, Grocery, Hobby & Leisure (largest e-commerce category at ~25% of market revenue). Bestsellers path: amazon.eg/-/en/gp/bestsellers (and /ar/ for Arabic).

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT verified live: amazon.eg returns HTTP 503 to plain server fetches and the H10 KB returns 403 — confirming aggressive bot-blocking. None of Helium 10 / Jungle Scout / Keepa / SmartScout cover the Egypt marketplace, so ALL data must be self-scraped (Best Sellers, Movers & Shakers, New Releases, search results, product pages) and ALL sales numbers must be ESTIMATED via a BSR→units model — there is no ground-truth sales feed to validate against.

CHART TYPES to standardize on: dual-Y time-series line (price+BSR+units) for product detail; horizontal bars / ranked list with delta arrows for movers; sparklines inside grid cells for trend columns; donut or treemap for category/brand share; heat-strip or small-multiples bars for 12-month seasonality; scatter (demand vs competition) for the opportunity quadrant. Recommend a single charting lib (Recharts or visx) for consistency, with restrained motion.

researchDimensions.topic: Legal/ToS risk of scraping amazon.eg public pages for personal product-sourcing (free/no-paid-API strategy)
researchDimensions.summary: Scraping amazon.eg public product pages for your own private sourcing decisions is a low-to-moderate, primarily contractual (not criminal) risk in practice, provided you stay logged out, rate-limit hard, and never republish or resell the data. The binding constraint is Amazon's Conditions of Use, which explicitly bans "any collection and use of any product listings, descriptions, or prices" and "any use of data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools" — so scraping is a clear ToS breach even when the pages are public. Criminal/CFAA exposure for scraping logged-out public pages is weak in the US after hiQ v. LinkedIn (violating ToS alone ≠ "without authorization"), but the Nov-2025 Amazon v. Perplexity Comet dispute shows Amazon will aggressively assert CFAA + trespass the moment automation touches a logged-in account or "masquerades as human." The EU sui-generis database right is a republication/re-utilization risk, not a personal-read risk, and post-CV-Online it only bites if you extract a substantial part in a way that harms Amazon's investment. Egypt's Law 151/2020 (PDPL) is largely irrelevant to scraping prices/specs (non-personal data) and offers a natural-person personal-use exemption, but would apply if you harvest seller/reviewer personal data. Realistic enforcement against a single low-volume personal user is throttling/IP-block/account-ban, not litigation — the legal floor is "don't get sued/banned," and you control most of that with behavior.
keyFindings: Amazon Conditions of Use (the controlling contract, same text used on amazon.eg) grants only a limited license that expressly excludes 'any collection and use of any product listings, descriptions, or prices' and 'any use of data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools' without express written consent — so scraping product/price data is a ToS breach by definition, regardless of robots.txt or page being public.

amazon.eg/robots.txt: for User-agent: * it Disallows path families like /gp/cart, /gp/sign-in, /ap/signin, /gp/wishlist/, /gp/video/library, and most /-/ (allowing /-/en/) — it does NOT broadly disallow /dp/ or /gp/product/ listing pages to the generic crawler. Separately it carries an extensive named-bot blocklist set to Disallow: / (e.g., ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, ByteSpider, Scrapy). No Crawl-delay directive is published.

CFAA picture (US): hiQ Labs v. LinkedIn (9th Cir., reaffirmed 18 Apr 2022 on remand) held scraping PUBLIC data likely is not access 'without authorization' under the CFAA, and that breaching a site's user agreement alone is insufficient for CFAA liability. So scraping logged-out public amazon.eg pages has weak US criminal exposure.

hiQ caveat: the case ultimately settled Dec 2022 with a $500,000 stipulated judgment against hiQ for breach of LinkedIn's user agreement AND a CFAA violation tied specifically to using fake accounts / accessing password-protected pages. Lesson: public-page scraping survived; logged-in / fake-account / credentialed access did not.

Amazon v. Perplexity (cease-and-desist Nov 2025 + suit over the Comet agentic browser): Amazon asserted (1) ToS breach of its 'robots, data mining' prohibition, (2) CFAA 'computer fraud' because the agent 'masquerades as human browsing' ('trespass involves code rather than a lockpick'), and (3) trespass/unfair competition. Critically this involved automation acting on a LOGGED-IN user's stored credentials — the trigger that flips a weak CFAA theory into a viable one.

EU sui-generis database right (Directive 96/9/EC): protects a maker who made 'substantial investment' against extraction/re-utilization of a substantial part (qualitatively/quantitatively). Post CV-Online Latvia (CJEU C-762/19, 2021) the test centers on whether extraction harms the maker's ability to recoup investment — meta-search/aggregation that doesn't deprive the maker of redemption income is generally permissible. Reading pages privately is not 'extraction of a substantial part'; bulk-copying the catalog and republishing it is the risk.

Egypt PDPL (Law No. 151/2020), in force, Executive Regulations issued 2024/2025: applies to electronically processed PERSONAL data of individuals in Egypt, requires explicit consent, and has extraterritorial reach. It is largely orthogonal to scraping prices/specs (not personal data).

Egypt PDPL has a natural-person personal-use exemption ('data processed by a natural person for personal use') and an exception for accurate data used purely for informational purposes — both helpful for a private sourcing use case that avoids personal data.

Egypt PDPL penalties are real but aimed at personal-data misuse: processing personal data without consent is punishable by imprisonment (not less than ~3 months) and fines of EGP 500,000–5,000,000; if harm results, imprisonment not less than 6 months and fine EGP 200,000–2,000,000; administrative fines up to ~EGP 5m. Regulator: Personal Data Protection Center under MCIT. These bite only if you harvest seller/reviewer PII, not prices.

Governing law/venue: Amazon's Conditions of Use bind users to Amazon's chosen law/forum and reserve the right to terminate access and pursue breach remedies; the immediate real-world enforcement tool is technical (CAPTCHA, throttling, IP/device fingerprint blocking, account suspension), not a lawsuit, for low-volume personal scraping.

Net realism: for a single personal user pulling modest volumes of public listing/price data logged-out, the dominant risk is operational (getting blocked) plus a low-probability contractual/cease-and-desist risk; criminal and database-right exposure stay low UNLESS you log in/automate an account, use heavy volume, or republish/resell the data.

verifiedClaims.claim: Scraping amazon.eg public pages for personal product-sourcing use carries LOW legal risk, with the main real consequence being IP/account blocking rather than litigation.
verifiedClaims.evidence:
The claim is DIRECTIONALLY CORRECT but the "LOW" framing needs qualification. Adversarial assessment across three axes:

(1) ENFORCEMENT TRACK RECORD — supports the claim. There is NO documented case of Amazon (or anyone) suing an individual or small-scale operator for personal-use scraping of public product pages. ScrapeHero's own analysis (a paid-API vendor with incentive to overstate risk) provides zero documented cease-and-desists or suits against small scrapers and treats litigation purely hypothetically; the primary, near-universal real-world consequence is technical — IP bans, CAPTCHA challenges, account termination. Amazon's civil suits are described as "rare and expensive to bring, almost always reserved for commercial scrapers with public-facing products that Amazon views as competitive." So the claim's core assertion (blocking, not litigation, is the real consequence) is well-supported for personal use.

(2) ToS vs LAW distinction — critical nuance the claim glosses. Amazon's Conditions of Use explicitly prohibit "any use of data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools." That makes scraping a CONTRACT/ToS breach, NOT automatically illegal. US precedent has steadily narrowed the legal exposure: hiQ v. LinkedIn (9th Cir.) held that scraping public, no-login data is NOT "unauthorized access" under the CFAA; Meta v. Bright Data (N.D. Cal., Judge Edward Chen, Jan 23 2024) held that "The Facebook and Instagram Terms do not bar logged-off scraping of public data" — i.e., ToS that bind logged-IN users often don't reach logged-OUT public scraping. So for logged-out public pages, the realistic worst case is a contract claim, which Amazon does not pursue against individuals.

(3) EGYPT-SPECIFIC angle — net LOWERS criminal risk for this use case. Egypt's framework is Cybercrime Law 175/2018 and Personal Data Protection Law 151/2020. The Cybercrime Law penalizes UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS to systems/accounts (login-protected / hacking-type access), with imprisonment ≥1 yr and fines EGP 50k–100k+ — but that targets bypassing authentication, not reading public no-login pages. The PDPL (151/2020) applies only to PERSONAL data of "an identified or identifiable natural person"; public product/price/commercial listings carry no personal identifiers and fall OUTSIDE its scope. Per the ICLG 2025-26 Egypt analysis, no provision criminalizes scraping non-personal public website data. (Caveat: amazon.eg listings include third-party SELLER names and reviewer profiles, which CAN be personal data — scraping/storing those specifically would pull the PDPL into play.)

COUNTER-EVIDENCE that raises risk (why "partially-true" not "confirmed"): Amazon v. Perplexity (N.D. Cal., Judge Maxine Chesney, preliminary injunction issued March 9-10 2026) shows Amazon is NOW actively litigating against automated access — the court found "strong evidence" Perplexity's Comet AI agent accessed Amazon "without authorization" and that Perplexity tried to "conceal" its agents. This is the strongest current signal that Amazon's litigation appetite is rising. BUT it cuts against the personal-sourcing use case only weakly: the defendant is a well-funded AI company shipping a competitive public-facing product, and the legal hooks were CONCEALMENT/disguising the bot and degrading the shopping experience — not the mere act of reading public pages. It does NOT establish exposure for a private individual sourcing products for themselves.

CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH RISK RISES (from LOW toward MEDIUM/HIGH): (a) scale/volume high enough to degrade Amazon's service — courts treat this as independently actionable even for public data; (b) building a public-facing or COMMERCIAL product on the scraped data (resale of data, a competing price tool) — this is exactly the profile Amazon sues; (c) bypassing technical barriers — defeating CAPTCHAs, rotating IPs to evade blocks, fake/disguised user-agents, or using logged-IN sessions — this is the Perplexity "without authorization"/concealment hook and the kind of "access" Egypt's Cybercrime Law could reach; (d) scraping/storing PERSONAL data (seller identities, reviewer names/profiles) — triggers Egypt PDPL 151/2020 and GDPR-style exposure; (e) ignoring an actual cease-and-desist (post-notice scraping is what converts a tolerated activity into willful breach).

NET: For a genuinely personal, modest-volume, logged-out, non-redistributed product-sourcing use that respects blocks, "LOW legal risk, consequence is blocking not litigation" is a fair and well-grounded characterization. The honest correction is that it is LOW *because of how narrow that use is*, not because scraping is broadly safe — and it is a ToS breach throughout (Amazon can terminate the account at will), with risk escalating sharply on scale, commercialization, barrier-bypassing, or personal-data capture.

(3) I did not retrieve amazon.eg's localized Conditions of Use directly; the data-mining prohibition is confirmed from Amazon's US Conditions of Use, and no evidence suggests amazon.eg differs, but the exact Egyptian-localized terms are NOT VERIFIED. verifiedClaims.claim: "BSR-derived sales signals and autocomplete-derived demand are accurate enough to guide real buying decisions." (Evaluated for a FREE/scraping-only data strategy on amazon.eg / Amazon Egypt, with NO paid-tool calibration.)
verifiedClaims.evidence:
VERDICT IN ONE LINE: As ORDINAL / relative signals these are usable for screening; as ABSOLUTE unit-sales numbers driving a buy quantity they are NOT reliable — and on amazon.eg specifically the error is materially worse than the published US/EU benchmarks because there is no calibration data, so unqualified numeric estimates would mislead.

PILLAR 1 — BSR -> sales accuracy (the published benchmarks are an UPPER bound, not your case):
- BSR is reverse-engineered and category-RELATIVE, not absolute. Independent write-ups state every estimator "is reverse-engineering sales from BSR," and the SAME rank maps to wildly different volumes by category: rank ~5,000 ≈ ~300 units/mo in Kitchen & Dining vs ~30 units/mo in Industrial & Scientific (a 10x spread for identical BSR). Source: bagengine.com, sellersprite.com. So a raw BSR with no per-category, per-marketplace calibration curve carries an inherent order-of-magnitude ambiguity.
- Vendor-reported accuracy (self-reported, marketing): Jungle Scout claims 15.9% overall error (~84% accuracy, improved from 25.4%); Helium 10 claims ~89.6% accuracy on a ~29,906-product July-2024 set vs Jungle Scout 60% in the SAME Helium-10-run study. These two vendors disagree by ~30 percentage points on each other, which itself shows the "accuracy" figure is method- and panel-dependent, not a property of BSR.
- The failure mode that matters for sourcing: LOW-VOLUME items. Independent testing found items selling <100 units/mo "especially unreliable, sometimes showing estimates that were double or half the actual figure" (i.e., ±100% — a 2x error band). Most new-seller candidate niches ARE low-volume, so the realistic error in the decision-relevant regime is far worse than the headline ~16-20%.
- Even the optimistic guidance says treat a "500 units" estimate as a 400–600 PLANNING RANGE (±20%) — and that is WITH a calibrated paid tool on a supported US marketplace.

PILLAR 2 — Autocomplete -> demand is ORDINAL and INFERENTIAL, never a quantity:
- Amazon publishes NO search-volume numbers. Autocomplete ordering reflects popularity + relevance signals; "lower autocomplete position = higher volume" is an INFERENCE, not quantified data (keywordtool.io, selfpublishingtitans.com, sellersessions.com).
- Documented bias: PPC/ad spend can inflate a phrase's visibility; a suggestion can be popular yet fiercely competitive or a poor product-fit. Autocomplete must be cross-checked against SERP depth, rank, and conversion — Amazon-native signals "should be used together," and treating one in isolation (or treating social/Google trends as Amazon demand) is a named common mistake. So autocomplete supports "is there interest / what words do buyers use" (qualitative, real buyer-intent language) but cannot answer "how many units/month" (quantitative).

PILLAR 3 — WHY EGYPT IS THE WORST CASE (the decisive point for this product):
- The paid tools that DEFINE the published accuracy numbers do not even cover this market the same way. Jungle Scout EXPLICITLY cannot connect to amazon.eg ("You can't connect Jungle Scout to ... Egypt"), and its Sales Estimator excludes the entire MENA/thin cluster: "All except NL, TR, SA, AE, AU, SG, BR, BE" — i.e., NO Sales Estimator for UAE (AE), Saudi (SA), Turkey (TR) (revenuegeeks.com). Helium 10 lists Egypt among "supported" marketplaces but support = the tool runs; it does NOT mean the BSR->units model is trained on Egyptian sales panels.
- The mechanism of every estimator is a learned BSR->units mapping fitted to a PANEL of known-sales products. That panel is overwhelmingly US/EU. amazon.eg is a young, lower-liquidity marketplace: fewer reviews per rank, sparser catalog per sub-category, more volatile/sparse BSR, and far fewer panel products to fit the curve. Therefore: (a) any US/EU BSR->units curve is mis-transferred to Egypt, and (b) you cannot even measure your own error because there is no ground-truth panel. Net: the realistic absolute-units error on amazon.eg is plausibly ≥2x in either direction across most niches (worse than the <100-unit/mo ±100% finding, which was measured on a CALIBRATED tool on a SUPPORTED market) — and this is NOT VERIFIED with an Egypt-specific study because none appears to exist publicly.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR REAL BUYING DECISIONS:
- SAFE uses (the signals ARE good enough for these): relative ranking of candidates within the SAME amazon.eg sub-category; direction/trend of a single ASIN's BSR over time (scraped repeatedly); presence/absence of buyer interest from autocomplete; competitive density from SERP. These are ordinal and survive the calibration gap.
- UNSAFE uses (will mislead): converting BSR to a specific units/month figure to size an order; converting autocomplete position to a demand quantity; comparing estimates ACROSS categories; any payback/ROI/units-to-stock math that consumes a point estimate as if it were a measured number. On amazon.eg these are the decisions most likely to cause a bad purchase.

HOW THE PRODUCT MUST COMMUNICATE UNCERTAINTY (so it never misleads):
1) Never show a single number. Show a wide RANGE with an explicit confidence band, and on Egypt widen it deliberately (e.g., display "~X units/mo, but realistically 0.3x–3x — Egypt: low confidence" rather than "500 units/mo"). Lead with the range, not the midpoint.
2) Label every estimate ESTIMATED / DERIVED / UNCALIBRATED, with a per-signal confidence tier (e.g., High = direct scraped fact like price/review-count; Medium = within-category ordinal rank; Low = BSR->units and autocomplete->demand on Egypt). Color/badge it.
3) Separate FACTS from INFERENCES in the UI. Scraped facts (price, BSR value, review count, # of sellers, autocomplete strings) go in one column; modeled inferences (units/mo, revenue, "demand score") go in a visually distinct, caveated column.
4) Force ordinal framing for decisions. Present "Candidate A ranks higher than B within Kitchen on amazon.eg" rather than absolute units; disable / hard-warn on cross-category numeric comparison.
5) State the calibration gap explicitly and persistently: a standing notice that "amazon.eg sales estimates are not calibrated against known Egyptian sales data; treat all unit/revenue figures as rough magnitude only," not buried in a tooltip.
6) Require corroboration before a "buy" nudge. Gate any green/positive recommendation on multiple agreeing signals (rising BSR trend + autocomplete presence + reasonable SERP competition + sustained over repeated scrapes), and show how many independent signals agree.
7) Show data freshness/volatility. Because Egyptian BSR is sparse/volatile, display last-scraped time and a stability indicator; flag single-snapshot BSR as low-trust and prefer multi-day scraped trends.
8) Never auto-compute downstream financials from a point estimate. If you show ROI/units-to-order, propagate the full range (worst/expected/best) and label the worst case prominently so the user sizes orders against the downside.

HIGH that autocomplete carries no published volume and is ordinal/inferential. HIGH that Jungle Scout cannot connect to amazon.eg and excludes the MENA cluster from its Sales Estimator (stated explicitly by revenuegeeks.com sourced from Jungle Scout's own compatibility table).\n\nNOT VERIFIED / WEAKER POINTS: (1) No PUBLIC, independent, Egypt-SPECIFIC accuracy study of BSR->units exists that I could find in this search budget — the ">=2x error on amazon.eg" figure is a REASONED INFERENCE from (a) the measured ±100% low-volume error on supported markets, plus (b) the structural fact that Egypt has no calibration panel and thinner data; it is not a measured number. Treat it as a directional argument, not a benchmark. (2) Vendor accuracy figures (Jungle Scout 84%, Helium 10 89.6%) are SELF-REPORTED marketing; the Helium 10 study was run by Helium 10. They are mutually contradictory (each rates the other far lower), which I used as evidence that 'accuracy' is method-dependent rather than relying on either number as truth. (3) The Helium 10 KB page (the authoritative per-tool Egypt support matrix) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read directly; the claim that Helium 10 'supports' Egypt comes from secondary sources, and 'supported' there means the tool runs in that marketplace, NOT that its sales model is calibrated on Egyptian data — that calibration claim is my structural inference, not a vendor statement. (4) Amazon could change autocomplete/BSR behavior at any time; figures reflect ~2024-2026 reporting. (5) METHOD CAVEAT for a free/scraping strategy: scraping amazon.eg at scale may violate Amazon's ToS and is brittle (anti-bot, layout changes) — an orthogonal risk to accuracy that also argues for conservative, hedged presentation. # Suuq — Amazon Egypt Product-Research & Arbitrage-Sourcing Platform
## Institutional Product Specification (Free / Scraping-First Strategy)

**Document owner:** Product Director
**Date:** 2026-06-08
**Status:** Draft v1.0 (for engineering + design kickoff)
**Working name:** *Suuq* (سوق) — placeholder; "Souq" was amazon.eg's predecessor brand, so confirm trademark clearance before adopting.

---

> **READ-FIRST DATA-INTEGRITY DECLARATION (governs the entire product)**
>
> This platform is built **entirely on free, scraped, and undocumented-public-endpoint data**. There is **no paid data API** and **no ground-truth sales feed for the Egypt marketplace** (Helium 10, Jungle Scout, Keepa, and SmartScout do **not** cover amazon.eg). Two consequences are non-negotiable and are wired into every screen:
>
> 1. **"Most-selling" is an ordinal rank proxy (BSR), not a unit count.** Any unit/revenue figure is a *modeled estimate with wide error bars* and must be visibly labeled as such. Displaying "X units sold" as if it were fact is a **Critical defect**.
> 2. **"Most-searched" does not exist as a number.** Amazon publishes no search volume. What we surface is an **"Estimated Demand" 0–100 score** derived from autocomplete ordering + BSR — labeled honestly, never as "search volume."
>
> Every estimate carries a confidence chip, a freshness timestamp, and the raw evidence (BSR + snapshot time) so the user can audit it. This honesty is a **product feature and a legal posture**, not a disclaimer afterthought.

---

## 1. Vision & Positioning

### 1.1 One-line
**The first product-research and arbitrage-sourcing cockpit built specifically for amazon.eg — turning free public signals (Best Sellers, Movers & Shakers, autocomplete, product pages, reviews) into honest, EGP-denominated sourcing decisions, in Arabic and English.**

### 1.2 The gap we fill
The entire global research-tool industry (Helium 10, Jungle Scout, Keepa, SmartScout) **stops at the Egyptian border.** Egyptian and cross-border sellers/arbitrageurs sourcing into amazon.eg — the #1 marketplace in Egypt as of 2026, ahead of Noon and Temu — are flying blind: no BSR history, no demand signal, no EGP-aware profit math, no Arabic review intelligence. They currently improvise with manual browsing and spreadsheets.

### 1.3 Positioning statement
> For **Egyptian and MENA arbitrage sellers and sourcing agents** who need to decide *what to buy and resell on amazon.eg*, **Suuq** is a **product-research and profit-analysis platform** that **surfaces selling/rising/demand signals and computes real EGP margins from free public data** — unlike **Helium 10 / Jungle Scout / Keepa**, which **do not support the Egypt marketplace at all**, and unlike **manual browsing**, which gives no history, no math, and no Arabic sentiment.

### 1.4 What we are NOT (scope guardrails)
- **Not a seller-account automation tool.** We never log into a user's Amazon account, never act on stored credentials, never place orders. (This is both a legal line — see §11 — and a trust line.)
- **Not a "guaranteed sales numbers" tool.** We sell *decision support under honest uncertainty*, not false precision.
- **Not a data reseller.** Scraped data is a private decision cache for the logged-in user; we do not republish or expose raw Amazon content as an open API (EU database-right + Amazon ToS line, §11).
- **Not a live-trading / financial-instrument tool.** (Despite shared house design tooling, this is a commerce research app.)

### 1.5 Strategic moat
1. **Egypt-only focus** — nobody else has the data here; the moat *accrues over time* because BSR/price history can only be built by snapshotting from day one (Keepa-quality charts are a function of how early we started).
2. **Honest-estimate methodology** — defensible metrics (rank-velocity, autocomplete-derived demand) that we can explain and stand behind.
3. **EGP + Arabic-native** — the profit calculator encodes Egypt's exact referral/FBA/VAT rules; sentiment understands Egyptian dialect + Franco-Arabic. These are deep, locale-specific investments competitors won't replicate for a "small" market.

---

## 2. Target Users & Jobs-to-be-Done

### 2.1 Primary personas

**P1 — "Karim," the Egyptian arbitrage seller (core user).**
Sells on amazon.eg via FBA/Easy Ship; sources locally and via import. Phone-first, bilingual (thinks in Arabic, reads English product specs). Cash-flow sensitive, ROI-obsessed. *JTBD:* "When I have capital to deploy this week, help me find a product I can buy and resell on amazon.eg at a margin that's actually worth it after every Egyptian fee and VAT — and tell me how confident I should be."

**P2 — "Mona," the sourcing agent / VA.**
Researches products on behalf of multiple sellers. Needs to triage hundreds of candidates fast, export shortlists, and justify picks. *JTBD:* "Help me screen the whole catalog down to a defensible shortlist with the numbers attached, and let me hand it off as a clean CSV/Excel."

**P3 — "Tarek," the rising-trend hunter / dropshipper.**
Chases momentum — wants what's *climbing* before it's saturated. *JTBD:* "Show me what's rising on amazon.eg in the last 24h/7d that isn't already crowded, so I can move first."

### 2.2 Secondary personas
- **P4 — Small brand owner / private-label seller** monitoring their own ASINs + competitors (watchlists, alerts, brand-gating awareness).
- **P5 — Category analyst / agency** building market views (category explorer, brand/seller intel, export).

### 2.3 Core jobs-to-be-done (mapped to features)

## 3. Data Source Map (the spine of the product)

Every feature in §5 cites one of these sources. This table is the canonical reference for *what is real, what is modeled, and what the free/scraping limit is.*

No BSR number, brand, or seller on the card. Thin EG categories may return **<50 items**. Browse-node IDs not published → must harvest from live left-nav. |

Confirms momentum, not volume. Path existence on .eg beyond bestsellers **not fully verified** — confirm live. |

Legal/ToS-clean fallback for catalog fields only. |

## 4. System Architecture (free-stack summary, informs features)

*Engineering detail lives in a separate tech spec; this is the product-relevant shape.*

- **Scraper tier (Crawlee + TypeScript):** Cheerio HTTP path first (cheap), Playwright + stealth fallback only for JS-gated/blocked pages. TLS impersonation (curl_cffi-equivalent) is the #1 free anti-block lever (~2% → ~94% success). Poisson-jittered pacing (~1 req / 4–6s, single warm IP), aggressive caching, exponential backoff + kill-switch on CAPTCHA. Residential/Egypt IP is effectively mandatory for sustained volume — a true $0 plan is fragile; budget ~$2–5/mo residential as the first paid upgrade. Firecrawl free tier (1,000 credits/mo, stealth = 5/page) as a managed bridge.
- **Scheduler:** BullMQ + Redis (real host) or pg_cron / GitHub Actions cron (zero-infra, best-effort, 5-min floor). Workers run **outside** the web app process.
- **Store:** Postgres/Supabase. Immutable timestamped snapshots `(snapshot_ts, list_type, category_node, lang, rank, asin, bsr, price_egp)` power all history/derived metrics.
- **NLP service (CPU, batch/nightly):** HuggingFace transformers — MARBERTv2 (Arabic/dialect) + DistilBERT-SST2 / twitter-roberta (English), routed by per-review language detection; KeyBERT/BERTopic for themes. All free/open weights, ~1–2 GB RAM.
- **Web app:** Next.js (App Router) + shadcn/ui + Tailwind (logical properties for RTL) + Recharts. House rule: shadcn-first, restrained GSAP only (reduced-motion respected), tabular-nums, deltas use arrow+color (never color alone).

---

## 5. Full Feature List by Module

Legend per feature: **Data source** (from §3) · **Free/scraping limitation** · **Honesty/UX note** where the estimate must be labeled.

### Module A — Discovery (Best Sellers & Movers)

**A1. Best Sellers feed (daily / weekly / monthly).**
Ranked product lists per category and overall; toggle the **time window** (Today / 7d / 30d). "Today" = latest snapshot; weekly/monthly = aggregated/median rank over the window from our store (suppresses single-snapshot spikes).
- *Data source:* DS-BS (live list) + DS-DERIVED (windowed aggregation).
- *Limitation:* Amazon's own list reflects ~24–48h; true daily/weekly/monthly **roll-ups are ours**, only as deep as our history. Lazy-load means we must headless-render to get the full 50/100. Thin categories may show <50.
- *Honesty note:* "Most-selling" badge tooltip: *"Ranked by Amazon Best Sellers position (relative popularity), not unit sales."*

**A2. Movers & Shakers (rising) feed.**
Amazon's biggest 24h rank gainers per category, surfaced directly, with rank-change arrows + % badges.
- *Data source:* DS-MS.
- *Limitation:* Hourly refresh; momentum ≠ volume (a 30/day product can outrank a 200/day one). `.eg` path beyond `/gp/bestsellers` not fully verified — fall back to our own DS-DERIVED velocity if the path 503s/404s.

**A3. Sales-band indicator (ordinal, not units).**
Each product gets a **Very High / High / Moderate / Low** band derived from log(BSR) percentiles *within its category* from our snapshot history — never a cross-category raw-BSR comparison.
- *Data source:* DS-DERIVED + DS-MODEL.
- *Limitation:* Requires accumulated per-category history to set percentiles; cold-start categories show "Insufficient data."
- *Honesty note:* Band, not a number. Optional unit estimate is gated behind A4.

**A4. (Gated) rough unit/revenue estimate.**
Behind an explicit "Show rough estimate" reveal: `Daily ≈ A·BSR^B` with **category-specific, editable** coefficients, shown as a **range (±50%+)** with a **Low/Med/High confidence chip**, the underlying BSR, and snapshot time.
- *Data source:* DS-MODEL (power law) + DS-PD (BSR).
- *Limitation:* **No EG calibration** — coefficients are US/Books-derived; cross-category error ~5×; thin categories worse. **By construction "Not verified" for EG.**
- *Honesty note:* Label verbatim: *"Estimated — modeled from public rank, not actual sales."* Showing a bare "X units" point value = Critical defect.

**A5. New Releases / Most Wished For (optional, v2).**
If `.eg` exposes these paths (unverified), mirror as additional discovery feeds.
- *Data source:* DS-BS-family. *Limitation:* path existence unconfirmed on .eg.

### Module B — Demand (Estimated-Demand Keyword Explorer)

**B1. Estimated-Demand keyword explorer.**
Searchable, sortable table of harvested queries with a **0–100 Demand Score** (not search volume), 30d/90d trend sparkline, and the top ASINs each query surfaces.
- *Data source:* DS-AC (autocomplete) + DS-PD/DS-SR (matching products) + DS-DERIVED (trend).
- *Limitation:* Ordinal proxy only; needs browser-like session or empty results; English vs Arabic via `lop`. Personalization risk if session IDs included.
- *Honesty note:* Column header tooltip: *"Relative interest from autocomplete ordering — not real search volume."*

**B2. Demand-score methodology (transparent).**
`DemandScore = 0.5·normalized_autocomplete_score + 0.3·normalized_inverse_median_BSR_of_top_matches + 0.2·normalized_riser_signal`. Autocomplete score = base 100 apportioned by the **prefix length at first appearance** × **position factor** (top=1.0 → tail≈0). An info panel exposes this formula to the user (trust through transparency).
- *Data source:* DS-AC + DS-MODEL.
- *Limitation:* Weights are heuristic, not empirically tuned to EG; presented as relative score.

**B3. Seed-expansion harvester (background).**
Iterates seeds (category names, brands, product nouns) × `[a–z, 0–9, core Arabic letters]` suffixes, dedupes, recurses on frequent stems; frequency = co-occurrence across distinct seed queries = relative-popularity signal.
- *Data source:* DS-AC.
- *Limitation:* ~350 unique suggestions/seed; throttle 1–3 req/s + jitter; soft (undocumented) rate limit.

**B4. Bilingual demand (AR + EN).**
Run harvest in both `lop=ar_EG` and English; show a language toggle and a "bilingual" merged view.
- *Data source:* DS-AC. *Limitation:* canonical Arabic `lop` value (`ar_EG` vs `ar_AE`) not fully verified — make configurable.

**B5. Keyword→product bridge.**
From any query, jump to its live SERP results (ASIN/price/rating/sponsored flag) to map demand to concrete sourcing targets.
- *Data source:* DS-SR. *Limitation:* SERP 503s to plain fetch → headless; sponsored noise flagged.

### Module C — Product (Detail + Reviews + History)

**C1. Product detail page.**
Hero (image carousel, title, brand, EGP price, BSR if present, avg rating, **total review count**, seller badges, availability) + spec block.
- *Data source:* DS-PD. *Limitation:* 503 risk; BSR often absent; selector drift (wrap each selector with fallbacks + null-rate alerting).

**C2. Review intelligence — count + actual written reviews.**
Total review count + the **actual review text** we can reach (deduped across star/sort passes), each with star, date, verified badge, helpful votes, detected language tag.
- *Data source:* DS-RV. *Limitation:* **Hard cap ~300–500 reviews free**; growing **login wall** for deep reviews; we show "Showing N of M (free-access limited)" honestly.

**C3. Sentiment (Arabic + English + Franco-Arabic).**
Per-review and aggregate sentiment (positive/neutral/negative), routed by language: MARBERTv2 for Arabic/Masry, DistilBERT/twitter-roberta for English; Arabizi transliterated before scoring; cross-checked against star rating (1–2★ + "positive" = flagged).
- *Data source:* DS-RV + DS-MODEL (NLP). *Limitation:* No amazon.eg sentiment benchmark exists → accuracy unverified until validated on ~200 hand-labeled EG reviews; sarcasm/code-switch hard.
- *Honesty note:* Show a "model confidence / coverage" indicator and the % of reviews successfully language-routed.

**C4. Pros/Cons + theme extraction.**
Extractive, deterministic: KeyBERT on positive-set → **Pros**, negative-set → **Cons/complaints**, each with a real evidence quote, mapped to fixed Egypt-relevant aspect buckets (**Quality, Price/EGP Value, Shipping/Delivery, Authenticity/Counterfeit, Packaging, Seller/Service, Battery, Sizing**); per-aspect % positive.
- *Data source:* DS-RV + DS-MODEL. *Limitation:* Quality scales with review count reachable (C2 cap); thin-review products yield sparse themes.

**C5. Historical BSR + price charts (Keepa-style).**
Dual-axis time-series: left = EGP price, right = BSR (lower=better); series toggles; range chips Day/Week/Month/3M/Year/All; BSR plotted on **log axis**; risers badged **"sustained" vs "spike."**
- *Data source:* DS-DERIVED (our snapshots). *Limitation:* **History only from launch** — no backfill; early charts are short; gaps where scrapes 503'd are shown honestly (not interpolated as fact).

**C6. Rating histogram.**
Per-star distribution from the detail page (logged-out-safe even when individual reviews are gated).
- *Data source:* DS-PD. *Limitation:* none significant; available even under review login wall.

### Module D — Search

**D1. Search by product name.**
Free-text (AR/EN) search → live SERP-backed results with ASIN/price/rating/review-count/thumbnail/sponsored flag; click-through to C1.
- *Data source:* DS-SR. *Limitation:* 503 to plain fetch → headless render; cache 15 min; sponsored rows labeled.

**D2. Search by ASIN / paste-URL.**
Paste an ASIN or `/dp/` URL to jump straight to product detail.
- *Data source:* DS-PD. *Limitation:* anti-bot per fetch.

**D3. Saved searches.**
Persist a query + filter set; re-run on demand or on schedule; diff against last run ("3 new products matched").
- *Data source:* DS-SR + DS-DERIVED. *Limitation:* scheduled re-runs consume scrape budget → capped per user-tier.

### Module E — Economics (Profit / Fee Calculator)

**E1. EGP profit/fee calculator (referral + FBA + VAT → margin & ROI).**
Two-pane: inputs (Sale Price *VAT-inclusive*, COGS, inbound shipping/unit, category, size-tier/weight/volume, fulfilment method FBA/EasyShip/MFN, months-in-storage, monthly subscription, units/month, ad cost/unit, returns %, VAT-registered toggle) → live result card (**Net Profit/unit, Margin %, ROI %, break-even price**) + a **fee waterfall**.
- *Data source:* DS-FEE (versioned config) + user inputs. *Limitation:* Inbound freight to EG FCs is **not published** → user-entered; FBA cells need spot-confirm; rates change → editable config with as-of date.

**E2. Egypt fee engine (the locale moat).** Encodes exactly:
- Referral: flat categories `max(rate·P, 5 EGP)`; **tiered** categories with EGP breakpoints (Electronics Accessories 15%≤1,000 + 8% above; Jewelry 19%≤5,000 + 5% above; Grocery 4%≤250 + 10% above, **no minimum**).
- FBA: EGP ladder by size-tier/weight with the **~350 EGP price-band** split (low/high column).
- **VAT 14% added on top of every Amazon fee** (the thing most calculators get wrong); customer prices are **VAT-inclusive** so a VAT-registered seller's true revenue = `P/1.14`; registered sellers reclaim input VAT on fees, non-registered don't.
- Storage ~4 EGP/cu.ft/mo; Pro-plan currently 0 EGP (promo).
- Break-even solved per VAT-registration status; **numerically (bisection)** for tiered categories; guard for "can never break even."
- *Data source:* DS-FEE. *Limitation:* per-category nuances (referral on item-vs-item+shipping) **not isolated for EG** — verify; VAT-reclaim treatment flagged "confirm with EG tax advisor."

**E3. Calculator ↔ product binding.**
Open the calculator pre-filled from any product (price, category inferred) for one-click profitability on a real ASIN.
- *Data source:* DS-PD + E2. *Limitation:* category→referral-rate mapping may be ambiguous for some listings → user confirms category.

### Module F — Intelligence (Opportunity & Scoring)

**F1. Opportunity Score (1–10).**
Composite of **demand** (BSR band + Demand Score) ÷ **competition** (active-seller count, review-count saturation, rating) × **economics** (margin/ROI from E1 defaults) × **momentum** (rank-velocity). Shown 1–10 with a breakdown of each driver's contribution.
- *Data source:* DS-DERIVED + DS-MODEL + DS-PD. *Limitation:* Inputs are themselves estimates → score is **relative, not absolute**; transparent breakdown required.
- *Honesty note:* Tooltip: *"A relative, modeled score combining estimated demand, competition, and margin — not a guarantee."*

**F2. Competition tier (Very Low → Very High).**

## 1. Executive Summary

The free/scraping strategy is **technically buildable but evidentiarily fragile**, and its fragility is concentrated in exactly the two requirements the user most likely cares about: "most searched" and "most selling." Live verification on 2026-06-08 produced three load-bearing findings that the build must be designed around:

- **Datacenter/$0 fetches of amazon.eg return HTTP 503 on the first request** (Best Sellers root and `/electronics` both confirmed). A pure $0, single-datacenter-IP recurring scraper is **confirmed non-viable** for a reliable feed.
- **The Amazon autocomplete endpoint accepts the Egypt marketplace ID but returns an EMPTY suggestions array for Egypt**, while the identical call for the US marketplace returns 10 rich, current suggestions. The "most searched" demand proxy via autocomplete is **not currently obtainable** for `.eg` through the documented endpoint.
- **BSR→units and autocomplete→demand are ordinal signals at best, and on amazon.eg they are uncalibratable** (no Egyptian ground-truth sales panel; the paid tools that define published accuracy figures do not cover Egypt). Any absolute "units sold/month" number is **misleading by construction**.

None of this kills the product, but it forces a **scope correction**: the app must reposition from "we tell you how much sells and what people search" to "we surface Amazon's own public Best Sellers / Movers & Shakers rankings, track them over time, and estimate relative demand — with explicit uncertainty." The profit calculator and the review-sentiment pipeline are the two **genuinely solid** pillars and should anchor the product's credibility.

**Overall Risk Rating: HIGH** (driven by data-accuracy and operational-sustainability risk, not by build complexity).

### The $0 envelope (sustainable cadence/volume)

**Confirmed-false claim:** "recurring scraping is sustainable at ~$0 without Amazon blocking it into uselessness." Live evidence: **503 on the first datacenter request**, because AWS WAF classifies by ASN in the first packet — a single VPS/cloud IP is flagged pre-HTTP. Datacenter single-IP success ≈ 10–20%; every free proxy tier (e.g., Webshare 10 free) is datacenter and inherits that failure.

**What $0 actually buys (honest envelope):**

| Parameter | Realistic $0 setting |
|---|---|
| Fetcher | `curl_cffi` (`impersonate=chrome`) for static fields — TLS match is the #1 free lever (~2% → ~94% on Amazon generally; Not verified on `.eg`). Headless (Playwright + stealth) only for JS-gated reviews/offers. |
| Egress IP | A **residential home connection used directly** (NOT cloud). A cloud/VPS IP is the harshest case (confirmed 503). Risk: a home IP can be CAPTCHA-walled or semi-banned for hours–days. |
| Cadence | 1 request / 4–6s with **Poisson jitter** (never uniform); ~10–15 req/min single IP, with long "reading" pauses. |
| Volume ceiling | **Planning estimate only: ~500–900 pages/day** single IP before reputation decay (explicitly **Not verified / not measured**). Treat as a few hundred pages/day to be safe. |
| Refresh discipline | Cache aggressively: price re-check 6–24h, static attrs weekly, BSR snapshot 1–4×/day same-hour. Caching is the highest-leverage free mitigation. |
| Managed free bridge | Firecrawl free tier = 1,000 credits/month (~1,000 normal or ~200 stealth pages); 10 scrapes/min; **does not roll over**. Good for small/bursty jobs, not a steady high-volume feed. |
| Scheduling | GitHub Actions cron (free, 5-min floor, best-effort timing) for daily/weekly snapshots; or BullMQ+Redis / Supabase pg_cron on a host. Never run scraping inside the web-app process. |

**Bottom line:** A truly $0 build can sustain a **small, slow, daily/weekly personal feed** — a few hundred cached pages/day from a residential connection, plus Firecrawl free as overflow. It **cannot** sustain a reliable, refreshed, multi-category, hourly feed. The "Keepa-style" price-history chart only accrues value slowly because **history is built from your own snapshots starting at zero**.

## 8. Legal / ToS Risk Summary + Guardrails

**Posture:** Scraping amazon.eg public pages for **personal** product-sourcing is **low-to-moderate, primarily contractual (not criminal)** risk — *because the use is narrow*. It is a **clear ToS breach throughout** (Amazon COU bans "data mining, robots…" and "collection and use of any product listings, descriptions, or prices"), so Amazon may terminate access at any time.

**Evidence calibration:**
- **Criminal/CFAA exposure is weak** for logged-out public pages (hiQ v. LinkedIn; Meta v. Bright Data, Jan 2024: "Terms do not bar logged-off scraping of public data").
- **Risk rises sharply** with: logging in / automating an account, barrier-bypassing (CAPTCHA-defeat, aggressive IP rotation to evade), high volume that degrades service, **commercialization/redistribution**, or scraping **PII** (seller names, reviewer profiles). **Amazon v. Perplexity** (preliminary injunction March 2026) shows rising litigation appetite — but the hooks were **concealment + logged-in agent + competitive public product**, not manual personal reading.
- **Egypt-specific:** Cybercrime Law 175/2018 targets **unauthorized (login/hacking) access**, not public no-login reads. PDPL 151/2020 applies only to **personal data** and has a **natural-person personal-use exemption** — prices/specs fall outside it; **seller/reviewer PII does not**. Penalties (EGP 0.5m–5m + imprisonment) bite only on PII misuse.

**Mandatory guardrails (build into the scraper, not the README):**
1. **Stay logged out.** Never attach Amazon account cookies/credentials. (This is the exact line that flipped Amazon's weak CFAA theory into a live claim in Perplexity.)
2. **Honor robots.txt programmatically.** Do not request the Disallowed families (`/gp/cart`, `/ap/signin`, `/gp/wishlist/`, most `/-/` except `/-/en/`). **Re-pull robots.txt verbatim before launch** (current copy was summarized, not captured).
3. **Do not send a recognized scraper/AI user-agent** (Scrapy default, ClaudeBot, GPTBot, PerplexityBot) — those sit in an explicit `Disallow: /` block. Use a plain browser-like UA; do not forge a specific human session.
4. **Rate-limit hard, back off on 503/429/CAPTCHA, and STOP on block** rather than escalating evasion.
5. **Scope fields to non-personal commercial facts** (ASIN, title, price, availability, rating count, BSR). **Skip seller legal names, reviewer handles, Q&A authors** to stay clear of PDPL/GDPR.
6. **Treat scraped data as a private local cache** with short TTL. **Never republish, resell, or expose raw Amazon content via an API/app** — this is the line the EU database right and the COU resale clause actually defend.
7. **Kill switch on any cease-and-desist or CAPTCHA wall.** Post-notice scraping converts tolerated activity into willful breach.
8. **Document personal, non-commercial intent** to support the PDPL personal-use posture.

**Hard line for the auditor:** the moment this product is **commercialized, redistributed, or scrapes PII**, the legal rating moves from Low toward **High** and the verdict for *that* version is **NO-GO** under the current plan.

## 9. Data-Accuracy Caveats & Required UI Uncertainty Disclosures

**Caveats (facts the data cannot support):**
- No true search volume exists; autocomplete (when populated) is ordinal only — and **currently empty for `.eg`**.
- BSR→units is uncalibratable for Egypt; absolute unit/revenue figures are order-of-magnitude at best, plausibly **≥2x error in either direction** (reasoned inference, **not** a measured EG benchmark).
- BSR is **category-relative** — never comparable across categories.
- Egyptian thin categories → volatile single-snapshot BSR; only multi-day trends are trustworthy.
- Sentiment runs on a **truncated, non-random** review subset (logged-out cap) and on models **not validated on `.eg` text**.
- Selectors are unconfirmed on live `.eg` HTML and **will drift** on Amazon redeploys.

**Required UI disclosures (treat any violation as a Critical defect):**
1. **Never show a single sales/revenue number.** Show a **range with a confidence band**, widened explicitly for Egypt (e.g., "~X units/mo, realistically 0.3×–3× — Egypt: low confidence").
2. **Label every modeled value** ESTIMATED / DERIVED / UNCALIBRATED with a per-signal confidence tier (High = scraped fact like price/review-count; Medium = within-category ordinal rank; Low = BSR→units and any keyword "demand").
3. **Separate FACTS from INFERENCES** visually — scraped facts in one column, modeled inferences in a distinct, caveated column.
4. **Force ordinal framing** ("ranks higher than B within Electronics on amazon.eg"); **disable/hard-warn cross-category numeric comparison**.
5. **Persistent calibration-gap notice**: "amazon.eg sales estimates are not calibrated against known Egyptian sales data; treat unit/revenue figures as rough magnitude only." Not buried in a tooltip.
6. **Show data freshness + volatility**: last-scraped timestamp and a stability indicator; flag single-snapshot BSR as low-trust; plot BSR sparkline (log axis) and badge "sustained" vs "spike."
7. **Flag low-data categories** ("few competing listings — rank is volatile").
8. **Keyword demand as a 0–100 relative score** with tooltip "relative interest, not search volume" — and if the autocomplete source is empty for `.eg`, **do not display the feature** rather than show zeros.
9. **Sentiment**: disclose "based on N of M reviews," show language-mix coverage, and the star-rating cross-check flag.
10. **Never auto-compute ROI/order-quantity from a point estimate** — propagate the full worst/expected/best range and surface the downside.
